descripcion_es: Government, parliament, elections and the European Union: the political vocabulary of the press.
resumen: Vocabulary for talking about governments, parliaments, elections and European institutions. Useful for discussing political news and presenting the institutional framework in English.

explicacion.texto: Watch out for words that look like Spanish but do not mean the same: “policy” is a specific policy (a measure or line of action), whereas “politics” is political activity in general. A “politician” is the person.

filas: government
the group of people who run a country (es: gobierno)
The government announced new measures.
prime minister / president
head of government / head of state in a republic (es: presidente del Gobierno / presidente de la República)
The Prime Minister resigned.
cabinet
the group of senior ministers (es: consejo de ministros, gabinete)
The cabinet met on Tuesday.
Parliament / the House
the elected law-making body / one of its chambers (es: parlamento / cámara)
The bill was debated in Parliament.
MP (Member of Parliament)
an elected member of a national parliament (es: diputado)
Several MPs voted against it.
bill / act
a proposed law / a law once passed (es: proyecto de ley / ley aprobada)
The bill became an act in May.
to pass / to reject a bill
to approve / to vote down a proposed law (es: aprobar / rechazar un proyecto de ley)
The Senate passed the bill.
general election
a national election to choose a parliament (es: elecciones generales)
A general election was called for June.
to run for office
to be a candidate for a post (es: presentarse a un cargo)
She is running for mayor.
to vote / voter / turnout
to cast a vote / a person who votes / the share of people who vote (es: votar / votante / participación)
Turnout was below 60%.
polls / opinion poll
the election itself / a survey of opinion (es: urnas / encuesta)
The party is leading in the polls.
coalition
an alliance of parties to govern together (es: coalición)
They formed a coalition government.
the opposition
the parties not in government (es: la oposición)
The opposition called for a vote of no confidence.
policy / politics
a specific measure or line of action / political activity (es: política (medida) / política (actividad))
Housing policy is a key issue.
to step down / to resign
to leave a post voluntarily (es: dimitir)
The minister stepped down after the scandal.
Member State
a country that belongs to the EU (es: Estado miembro)
All Member States must agree.
the European Commission
the EU executive body that proposes laws (es: la Comisión Europea)
The Commission proposed a new directive.
the Council of the EU
the body of national ministers of the EU (es: el Consejo de la UE)
The Council adopted its position.
the European Council
the meeting of heads of state or government (es: el Consejo Europeo)
The European Council met in Brussels.
MEP
Member of the European Parliament (es: eurodiputado)
MEPs approved the budget.
directive / regulation
an EU law that sets a goal for countries / an EU law that applies directly (es: directiva / reglamento)
Directives must be transposed into national law.
unanimity / qualified majority
agreement of all / a majority weighted by population and number of states (es: unanimidad / mayoría cualificada)
Tax matters require unanimity.
to enlarge / enlargement
to make bigger / the admission of new members (es: ampliar / ampliación)
Enlargement to the east took place in 2004.

items: “Elect” is used for people: “She was elected president”; for laws you say “pass” or “adopt”.
“Mayor” means alcalde, not “mayor de edad” (of legal age).
“Legislature” = the legislative branch or a legislative chamber; the period in office is a “term (of office)”.

ejemplos.frase: The bill was passed by a narrow majority.
ejemplos.traduccion: El proyecto de ley se aprobó por estrecho margen.

ejemplos.frase: Turnout was unusually high in the last election.
ejemplos.traduccion: La participación fue inusualmente alta en las últimas elecciones.

ejemplos.frase: The minister stepped down amid growing criticism.
ejemplos.traduccion: El ministro dimitió en medio de crecientes críticas.

ejemplos.frase: Member States have two years to transpose the directive.
ejemplos.traduccion: Los Estados miembros tienen dos años para transponer la directiva.

ejemplos.frase: Her grandfather was mayor of a small village in Galicia.
ejemplos.traduccion: Su abuelo fue alcalde de un pueblo pequeño de Galicia.

ejemplos.frase: The government's housing policy has been widely criticised.
ejemplos.traduccion: La política de vivienda del Gobierno ha recibido muchas críticas.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: The government's economic politics is failing.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: The government's economic policy is failing.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: A specific line of action is a “policy”.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: He presented himself to the elections.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Spanish “presentarse a las elecciones” is “run (for office)” or “stand for election” (British).

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: The parliament approved the law project.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Spanish “proyecto de ley” is a “bill”, and to “aprobar” a law is to “pass” it.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: The president of the government met the king.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: The Prime Minister met the King.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: The Spanish “presidente del Gobierno” is usually translated as “Prime Minister”.

ejercicios.frase: The new immigration ___ has divided the party.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the distinction explained at the start of the card: policy is a specific policy, a measure or line of action, whereas politics is political activity in general. The clue is “the new immigration ___”: it refers to a specific line of action on immigration, which is also new and countable. That is why the word is policy (immigration policy, housing policy, monetary policy).
ejercicios.traduccion: La nueva política de inmigración ha dividido al partido.

por_opcion.politics: Incorrect: politics is political activity in general (go into politics, Spanish politics), not a specific measure on immigration.
por_opcion.policy: Correct: a specific government policy or line of action, such as immigration policy.
por_opcion.politic: Incorrect: politic only exists as a formal, rare adjective meaning “prudent, shrewd” (a politic decision); it is not a noun.

glosario.definicion_l: a plan of action adopted by an individual or social group · a line of argument rationalizing the course of action of a government
an organization to gain political power · a gathering of people for pleasure

ejercicios.frase: He decided to go into ___ after university.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the card's distinction between policy and politics. The clue is the expression go into, meaning to take up or enter a profession or activity: it refers to politics as an activity and a career, not a specific measure. That is why the word is politics, which, although it ends in -s, normally takes a singular verb (Politics is a tough job).
ejercicios.traduccion: Decidió dedicarse a la política al terminar la universidad.

por_opcion.politics: Correct: political activity in general, the kind you choose as a career (go into politics).
por_opcion.policy: Incorrect: policy is a specific measure or line of action; you do not “go into a policy”.
por_opcion.political: Incorrect: it is an adjective (political party, political crisis) and a noun is needed here.

glosario.definicion_l: social relations involving intrigue to gain authority or power · the study of government of states and other political units

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with one word (proyecto de ley).
ejercicios.frase: The ___ will be debated in the House next week.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the table row “bill / act”: a bill is a proposed law while it goes through parliament, and an act is the law once passed. The clue is will be debated: if it is still going to be debated, it is not law yet, so it is a bill. The House is the short way of referring to a chamber of Parliament (for example, the House of Commons). Bill has other meanings (an invoice, a banknote in the US), but in a parliamentary context it is always a proposed law.
ejercicios.traduccion: El proyecto de ley se debatirá en la Cámara la semana que viene.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Law is a law already in force or law in general; what is debated in the chamber before being passed is a bill.
Act is the law once passed; if it is still going to be debated, it is a bill.
A calque of Spanish “proyecto de ley”: in English you do not say “law project” or “project”, but bill.

glosario.definicion_l: a statute in draft before it becomes law · an itemized statement of money owed for goods shipped or services rendered

ejercicios.frase: The Senate ___ the bill by 60 votes to 40.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the row “to pass / to reject a bill” and the card's note that elect is used for people, whereas for laws you say pass or adopt. The clue is the object the bill and the result of the vote (by 60 votes to 40): a chamber that approves a legal text passes it. Note also the formula by 60 votes to 40 (es: “por 60 votos contra 40”).
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: To approve a law is “pass”; “elect” is for people.
ejercicios.traduccion: El Senado aprobó el proyecto de ley por 60 votos contra 40.

por_opcion.passed: Correct: pass a bill is the fixed collocation for approving a proposed law in a vote.
por_opcion.approved of: Incorrect: approve of means “to think well of, to agree with” (I don't approve of his behaviour). Approve without of could be used, but pass is the proper expression.
por_opcion.elected: Incorrect: elect is used for people (She was elected president), not for laws.
por_opcion.voted: Incorrect: vote does not take a direct object like this; you say vote for or vote on a bill, not “vote the bill”.

glosario.definicion_l: the upper house of the United States Congress · assembly possessing high legislative powers

ejercicios.frase: Voter ___ fell to a record low of 45%.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the table row “to vote / voter / turnout”: turnout is the percentage of people entitled to vote who actually go and vote. The clue is voter ___ followed by a percentage (45%) and fell: what falls is the proportion of voters. Voter turnout is the usual collocation in the press, and a record low means “the lowest level ever”.
ejercicios.traduccion: La participación electoral cayó a un mínimo histórico del 45 %.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Participation exists, but it is not the word used for voting figures; the idiomatic word is turnout.
Written as two words it is the phrasal verb (to turn out: to attend or to prove to be); the noun is written as one word: turnout.
A false friend of Spanish “asistencia”: assistance means “help”. For voting figures you use turnout.

glosario.definicion_l: the group that gathers together for a particular occasion · a part of a road that has been widened to allow cars to pass or park
a citizen who has a legal right to vote

ejercicios.frase: She is ___ for mayor of Seville.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the table row “to run for office”: run for means to stand as a candidate for a post (run for mayor, run for president). The clue is the preposition for followed by the post, mayor, and the tense is ___ing, which shows an ongoing candidacy. Remember the card's note: mayor means alcalde, not “mayor de edad”. In British English you can also say stand for, without up.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “Run for” = to stand as a candidate for a post.
ejercicios.traduccion: Se presenta como candidata a la alcaldía de Sevilla.

por_opcion.running: Correct: run for + post is the expression for standing as a candidate.
por_opcion.presenting: Incorrect: a calque of Spanish “presentarse”. Present means to present something or someone (a programme, a report), not to be a candidate.
por_opcion.standing up: Incorrect: stand up means to get to your feet. In British English you say stand for mayor, but without up.
por_opcion.going: Incorrect: go for means “to try to get something” or “to choose”, but it is not the expression for standing in an election.

glosario.definicion_l: the head of a city government

ejercicios.frase: Unemployment is the main issue in Spanish policy today.
respuestas: Unemployment is the main issue in Spanish politics today.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the distinction between policy and politics. The clue is “Spanish ___”: it is not about a specific measure, but about the country's political life in general, what is debated in it. That is politics. Spanish policy would mean Spain's line of action in some specific area, and would also require saying which one (Spanish foreign policy). Issue, for its part, means “matter, question, problem” in public debate.
ejercicios.traduccion: El paro es el principal problema de la política española hoy en día.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Unemployment is the main issue in Spanish policy today.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: policy is a specific measure; political life in general is politics.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Unemployment is the main issue in Spanish politic today.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Politic is not a noun; political activity is politics, with -s.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Unemployment is the main issue in Spanish policies today.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Policies are several specific measures; for political life in general you say politics.

glosario.definicion_l: the state of being unemployed or not having a job

glosario.significado: asunto, cuestión, problema (en el debate público)
glosario.definicion_l: an important question that is in dispute and must be settled · one of a series published periodically
social relations involving intrigue to gain authority or power · the study of government of states and other political units

ejercicios.frase: Most ___ voted in favour of the new regulation.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the European Union table: MEP is the abbreviation of Member of the European Parliament. The clue is that they vote on a regulation, a European law, and that most needs a plural noun, hence MEPs with a lower-case -s and no apostrophe. Do not confuse it with MPs, who are members of a national parliament such as the British one.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Members of the European Parliament are “MEPs”.
ejercicios.traduccion: La mayoría de los eurodiputados votaron a favor del nuevo reglamento.

errores_previstos.explicacion: MPs are members of a national parliament; those of the European Parliament are MEPs.
The plural of an abbreviation is formed with -s and no apostrophe: MEPs. MEP's would be a possessive.
A calque of Spanish: it is not used in English; you say MEPs.

glosario.significado: reglamento (norma de la UE directamente aplicable)
glosario.definicion_l: prescribed by or according to regulation · an authoritative command

ejercicios.frase: Decisions on taxation in the EU require ___.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the row “unanimity / qualified majority” in the European table. The clue is grammatical: after the verb require you need a noun that works as the object, and unanimity is the noun. In the EU, tax matters still require unanimity in the Council, whereas most decisions are adopted by qualified majority.
ejercicios.traduccion: Las decisiones sobre fiscalidad en la UE exigen unanimidad.

por_opcion.unanimity: Correct: it is the noun, the object that require needs.
por_opcion.unanimous: Incorrect: it is the adjective (a unanimous decision); it cannot be the object of require.
por_opcion.unity: Incorrect: unity is the state of being united (of a group, of a country); it is not the voting rule that requires everyone's agreement.

glosario.definicion_l: everyone being of one mind
charge against a citizen's person or property or activity for the support of government · government income due to taxation

ejercicios.frase: The minister was forced to step ___ after the scandal.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the table row “to step down / to resign”: step down is a phrasal verb meaning to leave a post, to resign. The clue is the context (a minister after a scandal) and the structure was forced to step ___, which needs the particle. Step down is somewhat more neutral than resign and is very common in the press; down conveys the idea of stepping down from the post.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “Step down” = to resign, to leave a post.
ejercicios.traduccion: El ministro se vio obligado a dimitir tras el escándalo.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Step out means “to go out for a moment”; to leave a post is step down.
Step back means “to take a step back” or to distance yourself; it is not the fixed expression for resigning.
Step up means “to step forward, to intensify or to take on more responsibility”: exactly the opposite of leaving a post, which is step down.

glosario.definicion_l: disgraceful gossip about the private lives of other people · a disgraceful event

ejercicios.frase: The major of London opened the new bridge.
respuestas: The Mayor of London opened the new bridge.
The mayor of London opened the new bridge.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the card's note on mayor, which means alcalde. The mistake is one of spelling and meaning: major (with j) is an adjective meaning “main, important” (a major problem) or a military noun, a rank of officer. The clue is the meaning: whoever opens a bridge in a city is its mayor. It is accepted with or without a capital letter, because with the name of the specific post (the Mayor of London) a capital is common. Open here means “to inaugurate”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Alcalde is “mayor”; “major” means main or an army officer.
ejercicios.traduccion: El alcalde de Londres inauguró el nuevo puente.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The major of London opened the new bridge.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: major means “main” or an army officer; alcalde is mayor.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The Mayor from London opened the new bridge.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The post in a city is expressed with of: the Mayor of London. From would only indicate where the person comes from.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The alcalde of London opened the new bridge.
errores_previstos.explicacion: A mixture of languages: alcalde in English is mayor.

glosario.definicion_l: the head of a city government
British statesman who was prime minister from 1990 until 1997 (born in 1943) · of greater importance or stature or rank
a structure that allows people or vehicles to cross an obstacle such as a river or canal or railway etc.

ejercicios.frase: No party won a majority, so they had to form a ___.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the table row “coalition”: a government formed by several parties is a coalition, and the collocation is form a coalition. The clue is the first part of the sentence: if no party has a majority, the way out is to join forces. The other options are paronyms, words that look similar but have very different meanings, which you should not confuse when writing.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: A government of several parties is a “coalition”.
ejercicios.traduccion: Ningún partido obtuvo la mayoría, así que tuvieron que formar una coalición.

por_opcion.coalition: Correct: an alliance of several parties in order to govern (form a coalition).
por_opcion.collision: Incorrect: collision means “crash, clash” (of vehicles, of interests); it is not something formed in order to govern.
por_opcion.collation: Incorrect: collation means the gathering and comparing of data or documents, and in formal style a light meal; it has nothing to do with politics.

glosario.definicion_l: an organization of people (or countries) involved in a pact or treaty · the state of being combined into one body
the property resulting from being or relating to the greater in number of two parts; the main part · (elections) more than half of the votes

ejercicios.frase: The Greens are rising in the opinion ___.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the table row “polls / opinion poll”: an opinion poll is a survey of opinion, and in the plural, the polls, it also refers to the election itself (go to the polls, to vote in an election). The clue is the word opinion before the gap and the expression rise in the polls. Note that it is plural because it refers to the polls in general.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Surveys of voting intention are “opinion polls”.
ejercicios.traduccion: Los Verdes están subiendo en las encuestas.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Survey is a survey in general (market, satisfaction); after opinion the collocation is polls.
The plural is needed: you rise “in the polls”, in the opinion polls.
Pool means a swimming pool or a common fund; a survey is a poll, with a single o.

glosario.definicion_l: an inquiry into public opinion conducted by interviewing a random sample of people

respuestas: The Prime Minister called a snap general election
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the row “general election” and the collocation call an election. The clue for the order is the structure subject + verb + object: The Prime Minister (subject) + called (verb) + a snap general election (object). Inside the object, modifiers go before the noun: first snap, meaning “early, sudden”, and then general, which forms a fixed compound with election.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “Call an election” = to announce an election; “snap” = early.
ejercicios.traduccion: El primer ministro convocó unas elecciones generales anticipadas.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The Prime Minister called a general snap election
errores_previstos.explicacion: General election is a fixed compound and is not split: snap goes before everything, a snap general election.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The Prime Minister called a snap election general
errores_previstos.explicacion: A calque of the Spanish order (“elecciones generales”): in English modifiers go before the noun.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The Minister Prime called a snap general election
errores_previstos.explicacion: Prime Minister is a fixed compound with this order: Prime Minister.

glosario.definicion_l: a national or state election; candidates are chosen in all constituencies

ejercicios.frase: EU ___ must be transposed into national law.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the row “directive / regulation” in the European table and its example: directives set a goal and each Member State must incorporate them into its legal system, that is, transpose them. The clue is the expression be transposed into national law, which only makes sense with directives. Regulations, on the other hand, are directly applicable with no need for transposition, and treaties are ratified.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Directives are transposed; regulations are directly applicable.
ejercicios.traduccion: Las directivas de la UE deben transponerse al derecho nacional.

por_opcion.directives: Correct: directives are binding as to the result and must be transposed into national law.
por_opcion.regulations: Incorrect: regulations are binding and directly applicable in all Member States; they are not transposed.
por_opcion.treaties: Incorrect: treaties are primary law and are signed and ratified; they are not transposed like directives.

glosario.significado: directiva (norma de la UE que debe transponerse)
glosario.definicion_l: showing the way by conducting or leading; imposing direction on · a pronouncement encouraging or banning some activity

descripcion_larga_es: Vocabulary for talking about governments, parliaments, elections and European Union institutions in English: bill, MP, turnout, coalition, directive, qualified majority. It is essential for discussing the news and for presenting the institutional framework in an oral exam. It is hard for Spanish speakers because a single Spanish word, “política”, is split into policy and politics, and because there are false friends such as mayor and major.

contexto.que_es: It is the basic vocabulary of political life and institutions: bodies (government, cabinet, Parliament, the European Commission), people (MP, MEP, Prime Minister), processes (to pass a bill, to call an election, to run for office) and concepts (turnout, coalition, unanimity). It includes the key distinction between policy (a specific measure) and politics (political activity).
contexto.por_que_importa: Politics and the European Union appear constantly in the press and in any oral exam at B2 level or above, and even more so for a future Técnico Comercial. Using policy for politics, elect for pass or major for mayor produces sentences that a native speaker understands only with effort and that give away a calque from Spanish. Precise vocabulary gives you credibility when presenting an institutional topic.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: When discussing current affairs, explaining how a law is passed, describing an election or the division of powers in the EU. The signals are words such as vote, election, law, minister or Brussels. Spanish speakers tend to say “approve a law” (it is understood, but the idiomatic verb is pass) and to use “policy” for everything political.
